## Why This Is Asked

This question tests cross-account, cross-region SAP governance knowledge, including JIT (Just-In-Time) access, precise IAM and SCP mappings, and auditable change control in a real-world SAP ERP/DW deployment scenario.

## Key Concepts

- **Cross-Account Trust**: Establish trust relationships between AccountA (Production) and AccountB (DR) using IAM roles with external ID and MFA conditions
- **Region-Aware Replication**: Configure SAP HANA system replication across EU regions with proper network segmentation
- **Least-Privilege Access**: Map SAP authorizations to IAM roles via SCPs, ensuring operators only receive permissions required for their specific tasks
- **JIT Access**: Implement temporary credential access through AWS SSO with MFA enforcement, auto-expiring after defined sessions
- **Private Connectivity**: Use VPC Endpoint Services (PrivateLink) for SAP component communication, eliminating public exposure
- **Auditing**: Enable CloudTrail for API logging, AWS Config for compliance tracking, and Secrets Manager for credential rotation

## Code Example

```yaml
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: Cross-account SAP access role with MFA and PrivateLink
Resources:
  SAPCrossAccountRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: SAP-Operator-CrossAccount
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: arn:aws:iam::AccountB:root
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              Bool:
                aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent: 'true'
              StringEquals:
                aws:RequestedRegion:
                  - eu-central-1
                  - eu-west-1
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonEC2ReadOnlyAccess
      MaxSessionDuration: 3600

  SAPVPCEndpointService:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCEndpointService
    Properties:
      AcceptanceRequired: true
      NetworkLoadBalancerArns:
        - arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-central-1:AccountA:loadbalancer/net/sap-nlb/abc123
      PrivateDnsName: sap.internal.company.com
```

## Why This Is Asked
Observability is foundational for SAP workloads running on AWS; this question evaluates practical understanding of wiring together CloudWatch, CloudWatch Logs, and S3, along with a minimal Infrastructure-as-Code approach.

## Key Concepts
- CloudWatch Agent installation and metric collection
- Custom SAP HANA metrics via user-defined scripts
- CloudWatch Logs integration with S3 archival
- IAM roles for EC2 with CloudWatch and S3 permissions
- CloudFormation templates for role and alarm creation
- Basic alerting strategies and dashboard foundations

## Code Example
```yaml
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: IAM Role and CloudWatch Alarm for SAP HANA EC2
Resources:
  SAPCloudWatchRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: ec2.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: S3LogArchival
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogGroup
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource: arn:aws:logs:*:*:*
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - s3:PutObject
                Resource: arn:aws:s3:::sap-logs-archive/*
  CPUAlarm:
    Type: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
    Properties:
      AlarmName: sap-hana-cpu-high
      AlarmDescription: Alert when CPU exceeds 80%
      MetricName: CPUUtilization
      Namespace: AWS/EC2
      Statistic: Average
      Period: 300
      EvaluationPeriods: 2
      Threshold: 80
      ComparisonOperator: GreaterThanThreshold
      Dimensions:
        - Name: InstanceId
          Value: !Ref SAP HANALinux
      AlarmActions:
        - !Ref SNSTopic
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question assesses practical knowledge of patching SAP environments on AWS, evaluating understanding of downtime minimization, backup strategies, and safe rollback procedures using native AWS services.

## Key Concepts
- AWS Systems Manager Run Command for automated patch orchestration across EC2 instances
- SAP HANA backup to S3 with versioning enabled for point-in-time recovery
- Maintenance window planning and rolling update patterns
- AWS CloudWatch monitoring for validation and automatic rollback triggers

## Code Example
```yaml
Resources:
  SAPPatchAutomationRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: SAPPatchPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ssm:SendCommand
                  - ssm:GetCommandInvocation
                  - ssm:ListCommandInvocations
                Resource: '*'
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - s3:GetObject
                  - s3:PutObject
                  - s3:PutObjectVersionAcl
                Resource: arn:aws:s3:::your-backup-bucket/*
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ec2:DescribeInstances
                Resource: '*'

  SAPPatchLambda:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      Runtime: python3.9
      Handler: index.handler
      Role: !GetAtt SAPPatchAutomationRole.Arn
      Timeout: 300
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import boto3
          import json

          ssm = boto3.client('ssm')
          
          def handler(event, context):
              instance_ids = event['instanceIds']
              document_name = 'AWS-RunPatchBaseline'
              
              response = ssm.send_command(
                  InstanceIds=instance_ids,
                  DocumentName=document_name,
                  Parameters={'Operation': ['Install']},
                  MaxConcurrency='1',
                  MaxErrors='1'
              )
              
              command_id = response['Command']['CommandId']
              
              return {
                  'statusCode': 200,
                  'body': json.dumps({'CommandId': command_id})
              }
```

## Code Example

```javascript
// Sample Step Functions skeleton for cross-account patch pipeline
{
  "Comment": "Cross-account SAP patch pipeline",
  "StartAt": "TakeSnapshot",
  "States": {
    "TakeSnapshot": {"Type": "Task", "Resource": "arn:aws:lambda:region:acct:functionTakeSnapshot", "Next": "PatchOS"},
    "PatchOS": {"Type": "Task", "Resource": "arn:aws:states:::aws-sdk:ssm:sendCommand", "Next": "PatchSAP"},
    "PatchSAP": {"Type": "Task", "Resource": "arn:aws:lambda:region:acct:functionPatchSAP", "Next": "Validate"},
    "Validate": {"Type": "Task", "Resource": "arn:aws:lambda:region:acct:functionValidate", "Next": "Decision"},
    "Decision": {"Type": "Choice", "Choices": [{"Variable": "$.ok", "BooleanEquals": true, "Next": "RolloutAll"}], "Default": "Rollback"},
    "RolloutAll": {"Type": "Task", "Resource": "arn:aws:lambda:region:acct:functionPromote", "End": true},
    "Rollback": {"Type": "Task", "Resource": "arn:aws:lambda:region:acct:functionRollback", "End": true}
  }
}
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to architect cross‑region DR with SAP replication, DNS failover, IAM governance, and IaC.

- Route 53 health checks & DNS failover
- Cross‑region IAM roles and SCPs

## Code Example
```yaml
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Resources:
  DRHealthCheck:
    Type: AWS::Route53::HealthCheck
    Properties:
      HealthCheckConfig:
        Type: HTTP
        FullyQualifiedDomainName: sap-health.us-east-1.example.com
        ResourcePath: /health
        RequestInterval: 30
        FailureThreshold: 3
        Port: 443
  CrossRegionDRRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:root
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: DRScoped
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ec2:Describe*
                  - ec2:StartInstances
                  - ec2:StopInstances
                Resource: '*'
```
